cudaAccessPolicyWindow.doc:
Specifies an access policy for a window, a contiguous extent of memory beginning at base_ptr and ending at base_ptr + num_bytes.
Partition into many segments and assign segments such that. sum of "hit segments" / window == approx. ratio. sum of "miss
segments" / window == approx 1-ratio. Segments and ratio specifications are fitted to the capabilities of the architecture.
Accesses in a hit segment apply the hitProp access policy. Accesses in a miss segment apply the missProp access policy.

base_ptr.doc: Starting address of the access policy window. CUDA driver may align it.

hitRatio.doc: hitRatio specifies percentage of lines assigned hitProp, rest are assigned missProp.

missProp.doc: [CUaccessProperty](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gbf4806140e86865b45fc144941a6ced5) set for miss. Must be either NORMAL or STREAMING.

num_bytes.doc: Size in bytes of the window policy. CUDA driver may restrict the maximum size and alignment.

cudaArrayMemoryRequirements.doc: CUDA array and CUDA mipmapped array memory requirements.

alignment.doc: Alignment necessary for mapping the array.

cudaArraySparseProperties.doc: Sparse CUDA array and CUDA mipmapped array properties.

flags.doc: Flags will either be zero or `cudaArraySparsePropertiesSingleMipTail`.

miptailFirstLevel.doc: First mip level at which the mip tail begins.

miptailSize.doc: Total size of the mip tail.

cudaAsyncNotificationInfo_t.doc: Information describing an async notification event.

bytesOverBudget.doc: The number of bytes that the process has allocated above its device memory budget.

info.doc: Information about the notification. type must be checked in order to interpret this field.

overBudget.doc: Information about notifications of type cudaAsyncNotificationTypeOverBudget.

type.doc: The type of notification being sent.

graph.doc:
The child graph to clone into the node for node creation, or a handle to the graph owned by the node for node query. The
graph must not contain conditional nodes. Graphs containing memory allocation or memory free nodes must set the ownership
to be moved to the parent.

ownership.doc: The ownership relationship of the child graph node.

handle.doc: Conditional node handle. Handles must be created in advance of creating the node using `cudaGraphConditionalHandleCreate`.

phGraph_out.doc:
CUDA-owned array populated with conditional node child graphs during creation of the node. Valid for the lifetime of the
conditional node. The contents of the graph(s) are subject to the following constraints:

* Allowed node types are kernel nodes, empty nodes, child graphs, memsets, memcopies, and conditionals. This applies recursively
  to child graphs and conditional bodies.
* All kernels, including kernels in nested conditionals or child graphs at any level, must belong to the same CUDA context.

These graphs may be populated using graph node creation APIs or `cudaStreamBeginCaptureToGraph`. cudaGraphCondTypeIf: phGraph_out[0] is executed when the condition is non-zero. If size == 2, phGraph_out[1] will be executed when the condition is zero. cudaGraphCondTypeWhile: phGraph_out[0] is executed as long
as the condition is non-zero. cudaGraphCondTypeSwitch: phGraph_out[n] is executed when the condition is equal to n. If the
condition >= size, no body graph is executed.

size.doc:
Size of graph output array. Allowed values are 1 for cudaGraphCondTypeWhile, 1 or 2 for cudaGraphCondTypeIf, or any value
greater than zero for cudaGraphCondTypeSwitch.

type.doc: Type of resource, dictates which union field was last set.

cudaDevSmResource.doc:
Data for SM-related resources All parameters in this structure are OUTPUT only. Do not write to any of the fields in this
structure.

flags.doc: The flags set on this SM resource. For available flags see `cudaDevSmResourceGroup_flags`.

minSmPartitionSize.doc: The minimum number of streaming multiprocessors required to partition this resource.

smCoscheduledAlignment.doc:
The number of streaming multiprocessors in this resource that are guaranteed to be co-scheduled on the same GPU processing
cluster. smCount will be a multiple of this value, unless the backfill flag is set.

smCount.doc: The amount of streaming multiprocessors available in this resource.

coscheduledSmCount.doc: The amount of co-scheduled SMs grouped together for locality purposes.

flags.doc: Combination of cudaDevSmResourceGroup_flags values to indicate this this group is created.

preferredCoscheduledSmCount.doc: When possible, combine co-scheduled groups together into larger groups of this size.

reserved.doc: Reserved for future use - ensure this is zero initialized.

smCount.doc: The amount of SMs available in this resource.

cudaDevWorkqueueConfigResource.doc: Data for workqueue configuration related resources.

device.doc: The device on which the workqueue resources are available.

sharingScope.doc: The sharing scope for the workqueue resources.

wqConcurrencyLimit.doc: The expected maximum number of concurrent stream-ordered workloads.

cudaDevWorkqueueResource.doc: Handle to a pre-existing workqueue related resource.

canMapHostMemory.doc: Device can map host memory with cudaHostAlloc/cudaHostGetDevicePointer.

canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem.doc: Device can access host registered memory at the same virtual address as the CPU.

concurrentKernels.doc: Device can possibly execute multiple kernels concurrently.

concurrentManagedAccess.doc: Device can coherently access managed memory concurrently with the CPU.

cooperativeLaunch.doc: Device supports launching cooperative kernels via [cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g7c4cb6c44a6c4608da36c44374499b31 "Launches a device function.")

deferredMappingCudaArraySupported.doc: 1 if the device supports deferred mapping CUDA arrays and CUDA mipmapped arrays.

deviceNumaConfig.doc: NUMA configuration of a device: value is of type `cudaDeviceNumaConfig` enum.

deviceNumaId.doc: NUMA node ID of the GPU memory.

directManagedMemAccessFromHost.doc: Host can directly access managed memory on the device without migration.

globalL1CacheSupported.doc: Device supports caching globals in L1.

gpuDirectRDMAFlushWritesOptions.doc: Bitmask to be interpreted according to the `cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesOptions` enum.

gpuDirectRDMASupported.doc: 1 if the device supports GPUDirect RDMA APIs, 0 otherwise.

gpuDirectRDMAWritesOrdering.doc: See the `cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrdering` enum for numerical values.

gpuPciDeviceID.doc: The combined 16-bit PCI device ID and 16-bit PCI vendor ID.

gpuPciSubsystemID.doc: The combined 16-bit PCI subsystem ID and 16-bit PCI subsystem vendor ID.

hostNativeAtomicSupported.doc: Link between the device and the host supports native atomic operations.

hostNumaId.doc: NUMA ID of the host node closest to the device or -1 when system does not support NUMA.

hostNumaMultinodeIpcSupported.doc: 1 if the device supports HostNuma location IPC between nodes in a multi-node system.

hostRegisterReadOnlySupported.doc: Device supports using the `cudaHostRegister` flag cudaHostRegisterReadOnly to register memory that must be mapped as read-only to the GPU.

hostRegisterSupported.doc: Device supports host memory registration via `cudaHostRegister`.

integrated.doc: Device is integrated as opposed to discrete.

isMultiGpuBoard.doc: Device is on a multi-GPU board.

l2CacheSize.doc: Size of L2 cache in bytes.

localL1CacheSupported.doc: Device supports caching locals in L1.

luid.doc: 8-byte locally unique identifier. Value is undefined on TCC and non-Windows platforms.

luidDeviceNodeMask.doc: LUID device node mask. Value is undefined on TCC and non-Windows platforms.

managedMemory.doc: Device supports allocating managed memory on this system.

maxBlocksPerMultiProcessor.doc: Maximum number of resident blocks per multiprocessor.

maxGridSize.doc: Maximum size of each dimension of a grid.

maxTexture2DGather.doc: Maximum 2D texture dimensions if texture gather operations have to be performed.

maxTexture2DLinear.doc: Maximum dimensions (width, height, pitch) for 2D textures bound to pitched memory.

maxThreadsDim.doc: Maximum size of each dimension of a block.

maxThreadsPerBlock.doc: Maximum number of threads per block.

memPitch.doc: Maximum pitch in bytes allowed by memory copies.

memoryBusWidth.doc: Global memory bus width in bits.

memoryPoolSupportedHandleTypes.doc: Bitmask of handle types supported with mempool-based IPC.

memoryPoolsSupported.doc: 1 if the device supports using the cudaMallocAsync and cudaMemPool family of APIs, 0 otherwise.

mpsEnabled.doc: Indicates if contexts created on this device will be shared via MPS.

multiGpuBoardGroupID.doc: Unique identifier for a group of devices on the same multi-GPU board.

pageableMemoryAccess.doc: Device supports coherently accessing pageable memory without calling cudaHostRegister on it.

pageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables.doc: Device accesses pageable memory via the host's page tables.

pciBusID.doc: PCI bus ID of the device.

pciDeviceID.doc: PCI device ID of the device.

pciDomainID.doc: PCI domain ID of the device.

persistingL2CacheMaxSize.doc: Device's maximum l2 persisting lines capacity setting in bytes.

reservedSharedMemPerBlock.doc: Shared memory reserved by CUDA driver per block in bytes.

sharedMemPerBlock.doc: Shared memory available per block in bytes.

sharedMemPerBlockOptin.doc: Per device maximum shared memory per block usable by special opt in.

sharedMemPerMultiprocessor.doc: Shared memory available per multiprocessor in bytes.

sparseCudaArraySupported.doc: 1 if the device supports sparse CUDA arrays and sparse CUDA mipmapped arrays, 0 otherwise.

tccDriver.doc: 1 if device is a Tesla device using TCC driver, 0 otherwise.

texturePitchAlignment.doc: Pitch alignment requirement for texture references bound to pitched memory.

timelineSemaphoreInteropSupported.doc: External timeline semaphore interop is supported on the device.

totalConstMem.doc: Constant memory available on device in bytes.

totalGlobalMem.doc: Global memory available on device in bytes.

unifiedAddressing.doc: Device shares a unified address space with the host.

pArray.doc: Array of CUDA arrays corresponding to each plane.

pPitch.doc: Array of Pointers corresponding to each plane.

cudaEglPlaneDesc.doc: CUDA EGL Plane Descriptor - structure defining each plane of a CUDA EGLFrame.

numChannels.doc: Number of channels for the plane.

event.doc: The event to record when the node executes.
The event to wait on from the node.

width.doc: Width in elements when referring to array memory, in bytes when referring to linear memory.

flags.doc: Flags reserved for future use. Must be zero.

offset.doc: Offset into the memory object where the buffer's base is.

fd.doc: File descriptor referencing the memory object. Valid when type is [cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueFd](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg62ab2fcc2eb066702c3694148383749ed7c20291dcaa0968289cbdc1d1ef9884).

flags.doc: Flags must either be zero or `cudaExternalMemoryDedicated`.

handle.doc: Valid NT handle. Must be NULL if 'name' is non-NULL.

name.doc: Name of a valid memory object. Must be NULL if 'handle' is non-NULL.

nvSciBufObject.doc: A handle representing NvSciBuf Object. Valid when type is [cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeNvSciBuf](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg62ab2fcc2eb066702c3694148383749e6f8cf38ae8bb776722f29fe5f076bdcf).

key.doc: Value of key to acquire the mutex with.

timeoutMs.doc: Timeout in milliseconds to wait to acquire the mutex.

value.doc: Value of fence to be waited on.

binaryVersion.doc:
The binary architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major binary version \* 10 + the minor
binary version, so a binary version 1.3 function would return the value 13.

cacheModeCA.doc: The attribute to indicate whether the function has been compiled with user specified option "-Xptxas --dlcm=ca" set.

clusterDimMustBeSet.doc: If this attribute is set, the kernel must launch with a valid cluster dimension specified.

clusterSchedulingPolicyPreference.doc: The block scheduling policy of a function. See [cudaFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g61085e9f04656b92573af16072bbc78d "[C++ API] Set attributes for a given function").

constSizeBytes.doc: The size in bytes of user-allocated constant memory required by this function.

deviceNodeUpdateStatus.doc:
Whether the function can be updated on device. 1 means device node update is supported, 0 is unsupported or driver is too
old to check the value.

localSizeBytes.doc: The size in bytes of local memory used by each thread of this function.

maxDynamicSharedSizeBytes.doc:
The maximum size in bytes of dynamic shared memory per block for this function. Any launch must have a dynamic shared memory
size smaller than this value.

maxThreadsPerBlock.doc:
The maximum number of threads per block, beyond which a launch of the function would fail. This number depends on both the
function and the device on which the function is currently loaded.

nonPortableClusterSizeAllowed.doc:
Whether the function can be launched with non-portable cluster size. 1 is allowed, 0 is disallowed. A non-portable cluster
size may only function on the specific SKUs the program is tested on. The launch might fail if the program is run on a different
hardware platform.

CUDA API provides [cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1gef663acab61362749507747e30fb210d "Given the kernel function (func) and launch configuration (config), return the maximum number of clusters that could co-exist on the target device in *numClusters.") to assist with checking whether the desired size can be launched on the current device.

Portable Cluster Size

A portable cluster size is guaranteed to be functional on all compute capabilities higher than the target compute capability.
The portable cluster size for sm_90 is 8 blocks per cluster. This value may increase for future compute capabilities.

The specific hardware unit may support higher cluster sizes that’s not guaranteed to be portable. See [cudaFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g61085e9f04656b92573af16072bbc78d "[C++ API] Set attributes for a given function").

numRegs.doc: The number of registers used by each thread of this function.

preferredShmemCarveout.doc:
On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this sets the shared memory carveout preference,
in percent of the maximum shared memory. Refer to [cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerMultiprocessor](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cdc478150b5ec1689a2944aaf7e25a5685). This is only a hint, and the driver can choose a different ratio if required to execute the function. See [cudaFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g61085e9f04656b92573af16072bbc78d "[C++ API] Set attributes for a given function").

ptxVersion.doc:
The PTX virtual architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major PTX version \* 10 + the
minor PTX version, so a PTX version 1.3 function would return the value 13.

requiredClusterWidth.doc:
The required cluster width/height/depth in blocks. The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the
cluster dimensions is otherwise checked at launch time.

If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime should return cudaErrorNotPermitted.
See [cudaFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g61085e9f04656b92573af16072bbc78d "[C++ API] Set attributes for a given function").

sharedSizeBytes.doc:
The size in bytes of statically-allocated shared memory per block required by this function. This does not include dynamically-allocated
shared memory requested by the user at runtime.

cudaGraphEdgeData.doc:
Optional annotation for edges in a CUDA graph. Note, all edges implicitly have annotations and default to a zero-initialized
value if not specified. A zero-initialized struct indicates a standard full serialization of two nodes with memory visibility.

from_port.doc:
This indicates when the dependency is triggered from the upstream node on the edge. The meaning is specfic to the node type.
A value of 0 in all cases means full completion of the upstream node, with memory visibility to the downstream node or portion
thereof (indicated by to_port).
Only kernel nodes define non-zero ports. A kernel node can use the following output port types: `cudaGraphKernelNodePortDefault`, `cudaGraphKernelNodePortProgrammatic`, or `cudaGraphKernelNodePortLaunchCompletion`.

reserved.doc: These bytes are unused and must be zeroed. This ensures compatibility if additional fields are added in the future.

to_port.doc:
This indicates what portion of the downstream node is dependent on the upstream node or portion thereof (indicated by from_port). The meaning is specific to the node type. A value of 0 in all cases means the entirety of the downstream node is dependent
on the upstream work.
Currently no node types define non-zero ports. Accordingly, this field must be set to zero.

type.doc: This should be populated with a value from `cudaGraphDependencyType`. (It is typed as char due to compiler-specific layout of bitfields.) See `cudaGraphDependencyType`.

errorFromNode.doc: The from node of error edge when the topologies do not match. Otherwise NULL.

errorNode.doc:
The "to node" of the error edge when the topologies do not match. The error node when the error is associated with a specific
node. NULL when the error is generic.

result.doc: Gives more specific detail when a cuda graph update fails.

errNode_out.doc: The node which caused instantiation to fail, if any.

result_out.doc: Whether instantiation was successful. If it failed, the reason why.

cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdate.doc: Struct to specify a single node update to pass as part of a larger array to `cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdatesApply`.

field.doc: Which type of update to apply. Determines how updateData is interpreted.

isEnabled.doc: Node enable/disable data. Nonzero if the node should be enabled, 0 if it should be disabled.

node.doc: Node to update.

offset.doc: Offset into the parameter buffer at which to apply the update.

pValue.doc: Kernel parameter data to write in.

updateData.doc: Update data to apply. Which field is used depends on field's value.

graph.doc: Child graph node parameters.

reserved1.doc: Padding. Unused bytes must be zero.

fn.doc: The function to call when the node executes.

userData.doc: Argument to pass to the function.

syncMode.doc: The synchronization mode to use for the host task.

userData.doc: Argument to pass to the function.

extra.doc: Pointer to kernel arguments in the "extra" format.

kernelParams.doc: Array of pointers to individual kernel arguments.

sharedMemBytes.doc: Dynamic shared-memory size per thread block in bytes.

ctx.doc: Context in which to run the kernel. If NULL will try to use the current context.

extra.doc: Pointer to kernel arguments in the "extra" format.

functionType.doc: Type of handle passed in the func/kern/cuFunc union above.

kernelParams.doc: Array of pointers to individual kernel arguments.

sharedMemBytes.doc: Dynamic shared-memory size per thread block in bytes.

cudaLaunchAttributeValue.doc: Launch attributes union; used as value field of `cudaLaunchAttribute`.

clusterDim.doc:
Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b0563de2ec80489ee6a8010335db69abc3ff) that represents the desired cluster dimensions for the kernel. Opaque type with the following fields:

* x - The X dimension of the cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid X dimension.
* y - The Y dimension of the cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid Y dimension.
* z - The Z dimension of the cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid Z dimension.

clusterSchedulingPolicyPreference.doc: Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeClusterSchedulingPolicyPreference](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056cd9c1223027c72d7a5cdaf15483e438f). Cluster scheduling policy preference for the kernel.

cooperative.doc: Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeCooperative](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056f067f02ce2135e937c3dde1e9c62cfc6). Nonzero indicates a cooperative kernel (see [cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g7c4cb6c44a6c4608da36c44374499b31 "Launches a device function.")).

deviceUpdatableKernelNode.doc:
Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeDeviceUpdatableKernelNode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b0567e9bce67c8f264f4365c1591b0ec4f01) with the following fields:

* int deviceUpdatable - Whether or not the resulting kernel node should be device-updatable.
* cudaGraphDeviceNode_t devNode - Returns a handle to pass to the various device-side update functions.

launchCompletionEvent.doc:
Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeLaunchCompletionEvent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b0566ae5120e9f16194a1aaf16f2f88bbfaa) with the following fields:

* cudaEvent_t event - Event to fire when the last block launches.
* int flags - Event record flags, see `cudaEventRecordWithFlags`. Does not accept `cudaEventRecordExternal`.

preferredClusterDim.doc:
Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributePreferredClusterDimension](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056606609f73e12c84ccee8da7ee195a735) that represents the desired preferred cluster dimensions for the kernel. Opaque type with the following fields:

* x - The X dimension of the preferred cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid X dimension, and must be a multiple
  of the x field of [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::clusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue_1cba61aeaa1e8853e24cdb490c5c65665).
* y - The Y dimension of the preferred cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid Y dimension, and must be a multiple
  of the y field of [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::clusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue_1cba61aeaa1e8853e24cdb490c5c65665).
* z - The Z dimension of the preferred cluster, in blocks. Must be equal to the z field of [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::clusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue_1cba61aeaa1e8853e24cdb490c5c65665).

priority.doc: Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributePriority](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b05678f4b9132edfc2b8799b9cf16c1020c9). Execution priority of the kernel.

programmaticEvent.doc:
Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticEvent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056690bb55d13016cd9dfd841d467388773) with the following fields:

```text
* cudaEvent_t event - Event to fire when all blocks trigger it.
* int flags; - Event record flags, see `cudaEventRecordWithFlags`. Does not accept `cudaEventRecordExternal`.
* int triggerAtBlockStart - If this is set to non-0, each block launch will automatically trigger the event.
```

sharedMemoryMode.doc: Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeSharedMemoryMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056445c144f777a4306508cb45cdb49a341). See `cudaSharedMemoryMode` for acceptable values.

syncPolicy.doc: Value of launch attribute [cudaLaunchAttributeSynchronizationPolicy](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b05697a48816036826f84b85dc52bc7bc42b). cudaSynchronizationPolicy for work queued up in this stream.

dynamicSmemBytes.doc: Dynamic shared-memory size per thread block in bytes.

cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainMap.doc:
Memory Synchronization Domain map

See `cudaLaunchMemSyncDomain`.

By default, kernels are launched in domain 0. Kernel launched with [cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainRemote](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggafb98f7ea7b0397ed6503780f3e672d5ac477b14c4ce022e029a4c2523eaeec2) will have a different domain ID. User may also alter the domain ID with `cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainMap` for a specific stream / graph node / kernel launch. See [cudaLaunchAttributeMemSyncDomainMap](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggfc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056fef6b4fb87bd2e289180c2ca5805094d).

Domain ID range is available through [cudaDevAttrMemSyncDomainCount](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cd82ae431cc82ee71d008b4e8e9cac06ab).

default_.doc: The default domain ID to use for designated kernels.

remote.doc: The remote domain ID to use for designated kernels.

flags.doc: CUmemProt accessibility flags to set on the request.

location.doc: Location on which the request is to change it's accessibility.

accessDescs.doc: in: number of memory access descriptors. Must not exceed the number of GPUs.

bytesize.doc: in: size in bytes of the requested allocation.

dptr.doc: out: address of the allocation returned by CUDA.

poolProps.doc: in: location where the allocation should reside (specified in location). handleTypes must be [cudaMemHandleTypeNone](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggabde707dfb8a602b917e0b177f77f365fed45251c1591431e1b9da28c1a04191). IPC is not supported. in: array of memory access descriptors. Used to describe peer GPU access.

cudaMemLocation.doc:
Specifies a memory location.

To specify a gpu, set type = [cudaMemLocationTypeDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg2279aa08666f329f3ba4afe397fa60f0e479b8710f3c5270117ee9d8cf5868d4) and set id = the gpu's device ordinal. To specify a cpu NUMA node, set type = [cudaMemLocationTypeHostNuma](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg2279aa08666f329f3ba4afe397fa60f024dc63fb938dee27b41e3842da35d2d0) and set id = host NUMA node id.

type.doc: Specifies the location type, which modifies the meaning of id.

cudaMemPoolProps.doc: Specifies the properties of allocations made from the pool.

allocType.doc: Allocation type. Currently must be specified as cudaMemAllocationTypePinned.

handleTypes.doc: Handle types that will be supported by allocations from the pool.

maxSize.doc: Maximum pool size. When set to 0, defaults to a system dependent value.

reserved.doc: reserved for future use, must be 0.

usage.doc: Bitmask indicating intended usage for the pool.

win32SecurityAttributes.doc:
Windows-specific LPSECURITYATTRIBUTES required when [cudaMemHandleTypeWin32](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggabde707dfb8a602b917e0b177f77f3654b0a7c146b29154b18d39c5f3052f2f8) is specified. This security attribute defines the scope of which exported allocations may be tranferred to other processes.
In all other cases, this field is required to be zero.

cudaMemPoolPtrExportData.doc: Opaque data for exporting a pool allocation.

cudaMemcpy3DOperand.doc: Struct representing an operand for copy with `cudaMemcpy3DBatchAsync`.

array.doc: Struct representing an operand when cudaMemcpy3DOperand::type is [cudaMemcpyOperandTypeArray](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggda2d93832ded1a29fd7cb28a6261ee6c468b9e5daeac88a1cddc387310cb2952).

layerHeight.doc: Height of each layer in elements.

locHint.doc: Hint location for the operand. Ignored when the pointers are not managed memory or memory allocated outside CUDA.

ptr.doc: Struct representing an operand when cudaMemcpy3DOperand::type is [cudaMemcpyOperandTypePointer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1ggda2d93832ded1a29fd7cb28a6261ee6c395369a66615a9cacf1a734334859a67).

rowLength.doc: Length of each row in elements.

cudaMemcpyAttributes.doc: Attributes specific to copies within a batch. For more details on usage see [cudaMemcpyBatchAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g58cf0d0f10efd8c0748b1722ef9eb070 "Performs a batch of memory copies asynchronously.").

dstLocHint.doc: Hint location for the destination operand. Ignored when the pointers are not managed memory or memory allocated outside CUDA.

flags.doc: Additional flags for copies with this attribute. See `cudaMemcpyFlags`.

srcAccessOrder.doc: Source access ordering to be observed for copies with this attribute.

srcLocHint.doc: Hint location for the source operand. Ignored when the pointers are not managed memory or memory allocated outside CUDA.

ctx.doc: Context in which to run the memcpy. If NULL will try to use the current context.

elementSize.doc: Size of each element in bytes. Must be 1, 2, or 4.

pitch.doc: Pitch of destination device pointer. Unused if height is 1.

width.doc: Width of the row in elements.

cudaOffset3D.doc: Struct representing offset into a `cudaArray_t` in elements.

xsize.doc: Logical width of allocation in elements.

ysize.doc: Logical height of allocation in elements.

device.doc:
The device against which the memory was allocated or registered. If the memory type is [cudaMemoryTypeDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg13de56a8fe75569530ecc3a3106e9b6d30c8466dd99563e4b1a43dd27bf7c743) then this identifies the device on which the memory referred physically resides. If the memory type is [cudaMemoryTypeHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg13de56a8fe75569530ecc3a3106e9b6d9aa7478ab438d2dfb710c9100194a5be)[or::cudaMemoryTypeManaged](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gg13de56a8fe75569530ecc3a3106e9b6dbb20a4b61c559a4e7629fe60ac04b84e) then this identifies the device which was current when the memory was allocated or registered (and if that device is deinitialized
then this allocation will vanish with that device's state).

devicePointer.doc: The address which may be dereferenced on the current device to access the memory or NULL if no such address exists.

hostPointer.doc:
The address which may be dereferenced on the host to access the memory or NULL if no such address exists.

```text
Note:

CUDA doesn't check if unregistered memory is allocated so this field may contain invalid pointer if an invalid pointer has
been passed to CUDA.
```

height.doc: Height of the array in elements.

pitchInBytes.doc: Pitch between two rows in bytes.

width.doc: Width of the array in elements.

addressMode.doc: Texture address mode for up to 3 dimensions.

maxMipmapLevelClamp.doc: Upper end of the mipmap level range to clamp access to.

minMipmapLevelClamp.doc: Lower end of the mipmap level range to clamp access to.

mipmapLevelBias.doc: Offset applied to the supplied mipmap level.

normalizedCoords.doc: Indicates whether texture reads are normalized or not.

sRGB.doc: Perform sRGB->linear conversion during texture read.

CUDA_EGL_MAX_PLANES.doc: Maximum number of planes per frame.

cudaArrayColorAttachment.doc: Must be set in cudaExternalMemoryGetMappedMipmappedArray if the mipmapped array is used as a color target in a graphics API.

cudaArrayCubemap.doc: Must be set in cudaMalloc3DArray to create a cubemap CUDA array.

cudaArrayDeferredMapping.doc:
Must be set in cudaMallocArray, cudaMalloc3DArray or cudaMallocMipmappedArray in order to create a deferred mapping CUDA array
or CUDA mipmapped array.

cudaArrayLayered.doc: Must be set in cudaMalloc3DArray to create a layered CUDA array.

cudaArraySparse.doc:
Must be set in cudaMallocArray, cudaMalloc3DArray or cudaMallocMipmappedArray in order to create a sparse CUDA array or CUDA
mipmapped array.

cudaArraySparsePropertiesSingleMipTail.doc: Indicates that the layered sparse CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array has a single mip tail region for all layers.

cudaArraySurfaceLoadStore.doc: Must be set in cudaMallocArray or cudaMalloc3DArray in order to bind surfaces to the CUDA array.

cudaArrayTextureGather.doc: Must be set in cudaMallocArray or cudaMalloc3DArray in order to perform texture gather operations on the CUDA array.

cudaCpuDeviceId.doc: Device id that represents the CPU.

cudaDeviceLmemResizeToMax.doc: Device flag - Keep local memory allocation after launch.

cudaDeviceMapHost.doc: Device flag - Support mapped pinned allocations.

cudaDeviceSyncMemops.doc: Device flag - Ensure synchronous memory operations on this context will synchronize.

cudaEventDisableTiming.doc: Event will not record timing data.

cudaEventInterprocess.doc: Event is suitable for interprocess use. cudaEventDisableTiming must be set.

cudaEventRecordExternal.doc: Event is captured in the graph as an external event node when performing stream capture.

cudaEventWaitExternal.doc: Event is captured in the graph as an external event node when performing stream capture.

cudaExternalMemoryDedicated.doc: Indicates that the external memory object is a dedicated resource.

cudaExternalSemaphoreSignalSkipNvSciBufM.doc:
When the `flags` parameter of `cudaExternalSemaphoreSignalParams` contains this flag, it indicates that signaling an external semaphore object should skip performing appropriate memory synchronization
operations over all the external memory objects that are imported as cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeNvSciBuf, which otherwise are performed by default to ensure data coherency with other importers of the same NvSciBuf memory objects.

cudaExternalSemaphoreWaitSkipNvSciBufMem.doc:
When the `flags` parameter of `cudaExternalSemaphoreWaitParams` contains this flag, it indicates that waiting an external semaphore object should skip performing appropriate memory synchronization
operations over all the external memory objects that are imported as cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeNvSciBuf, which otherwise are performed by default to ensure data coherency with other importers of the same NvSciBuf memory objects.

cudaGraphKernelNodePortDefault.doc: This port activates when the kernel has finished executing.

cudaGraphKernelNodePortLaunchCompletion.doc: This port activates when all blocks of the kernel have begun execution. See also cudaLaunchAttributeLaunchCompletionEvent.

cudaGraphKernelNodePortProgrammatic.doc: This port activates when all blocks of the kernel have performed `cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion` or have terminated. It must be used with edge type cudaGraphDependencyTypeProgrammatic. See also cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticEvent.

cudaHostAllocPortable.doc: Pinned memory accessible by all CUDA contexts.

cudaHostRegisterMapped.doc: Map registered memory into device space.

cudaHostRegisterPortable.doc: Pinned memory accessible by all CUDA contexts.

cudaInitDeviceFlagsAreValid.doc: Tell the CUDA runtime that DeviceFlags is being set in cudaInitDevice call.

cudaInvalidDeviceId.doc: Device id that represents an invalid device.

cudaIpcMemLazyEnablePeerAccess.doc: Automatically enable peer access between remote devices as needed.

cudaMemAttachGlobal.doc: Memory can be accessed by any stream on any device.

cudaMemAttachHost.doc: Memory cannot be accessed by any stream on any device.

cudaMemAttachSingle.doc: Memory can only be accessed by a single stream on the associated device.

cudaMemPoolCreateUsageHwDecompress.doc: This flag, if set, indicates that the memory will be used as a buffer for hardware accelerated decompression.

cudaNvSciSyncAttrSignal.doc: When `flags` of `cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes` is set to this, it indicates that application need signaler specific NvSciSyncAttr to be filled by `cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes`.

cudaNvSciSyncAttrWait.doc: When `flags` of `cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes` is set to this, it indicates that application need waiter specific NvSciSyncAttr to be filled by `cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes`.

cudaOccupancyDisableCachingOverride.doc: Assume global caching is enabled and cannot be automatically turned off.

cudaStreamLegacy.doc:
Legacy stream handle

Stream handle that can be passed as a cudaStream_t to use an implicit stream with legacy synchronization behavior.

See details of the [synchronization behavior](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/stream-sync-behavior.html#stream-sync-behavior).

cudaStreamNonBlocking.doc: Stream does not synchronize with stream 0 (the NULL stream).

cudaStreamPerThread.doc:
Per-thread stream handle

Stream handle that can be passed as a cudaStream_t to use an implicit stream with per-thread synchronization behavior.

See details of the [synchronization behavior](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/stream-sync-behavior.html#stream-sync-behavior).

cudaDevResourceDesc_t.doc: An opaque descriptor handle. The descriptor encapsulates multiple created and configured resources. Created via cudaDeviceResourceGenerateDesc.

cudaExecutionContext_t.doc: An opaque handle to a CUDA execution context. It represents an execution context created via CUDA Runtime APIs such as `cudaGreenCtxCreate`.

cudaGraphConditionalHandle.doc: CUDA handle for conditional graph nodes.

cudaGraphDeviceNode_t.doc: CUDA device node handle for device-side node update.

cudaSurfaceObject_t.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA Surface object.

cudaTextureObject_t.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA texture object.

cudaAccessProperty.doc: Specifies performance hint with `cudaAccessPolicyWindow` for hitProp and missProp members.

cudaAccessPropertyStreaming.doc: Streaming access is less likely to persit from cache.

cudaAccessPropertyPersisting.doc: Persisting access is more likely to persist in cache.

cudaAsyncNotificationType.doc: Types of async notification that can occur.

cudaAsyncNotificationTypeOverBudget.doc: Sent when the process has exceeded its device memory budget.

cudaClusterSchedulingPolicy.doc: Cluster scheduling policies. These may be passed to [cudaFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/high-level-api.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g61085e9f04656b92573af16072bbc78d "[C++ API] Set attributes for a given function").

cudaClusterSchedulingPolicySpread.doc: spread the blocks within a cluster to the SMs.

cudaClusterSchedulingPolicyLoadBalancing.doc: allow the hardware to load-balance the blocks in a cluster to the SMs.

cudaComputeModeDefault.doc: Default compute mode (Multiple threads can use `cudaSetDevice` with this device).

cudaComputeModeExclusive.doc: Compute-exclusive-thread mode (Only one thread in one process will be able to use `cudaSetDevice` with this device).

cudaComputeModeProhibited.doc: Compute-prohibited mode (No threads can use `cudaSetDevice` with this device).

cudaDevWorkqueueConfigScopeGreenCtxBalan.doc: When possible, use non-overlapping workqueue resources with other balanced green contexts.

cudaDevAttrMaxThreadsPerBlock.doc: Maximum number of threads per block.

cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlock.doc: Maximum shared memory available per block in bytes.

cudaDevAttrTotalConstantMemory.doc: Memory available on device for __constant__ variables in a CUDA C kernel in bytes.

cudaDevAttrMaxPitch.doc: Maximum pitch in bytes allowed by memory copies.

cudaDevAttrMaxRegistersPerBlock.doc: Maximum number of 32-bit registers available per block.

cudaDevAttrKernelExecTimeout.doc: Specifies whether there is a run time limit on kernels.

cudaDevAttrIntegrated.doc: Device is integrated with host memory.

cudaDevAttrCanMapHostMemory.doc: Device can map host memory into CUDA address space.

cudaDevAttrMaxTexture2DLayeredLayers.doc: Maximum layers in a 2D layered texture.

cudaDevAttrConcurrentKernels.doc: Device can possibly execute multiple kernels concurrently.

cudaDevAttrPciBusId.doc: PCI bus ID of the device.

cudaEglResourceLocationFlags.doc:
Resource location flags- sysmem or vidmem

For CUDA context on iGPU, since video and system memory are equivalent - these flags will not have an effect on the execution.

For CUDA context on dGPU, applications can use the flag `cudaEglResourceLocationFlags` to give a hint about the desired location.

cudaEglResourceLocationSysmem - the frame data is made resident on the system memory to be accessed by CUDA.

cudaEglResourceLocationVidmem - the frame data is made resident on the dedicated video memory to be accessed by CUDA.

There may be an additional latency due to new allocation and data migration, if the frame is produced on a different memory.

cudaSuccess.doc:
The API call returned with no errors. In the case of query calls, this also means that the operation being queried is complete
(see `cudaEventQuery` and `cudaStreamQuery`).

cudaErrorInvalidValue.doc: This indicates that one or more of the parameters passed to the API call is not within an acceptable range of values.

cudaErrorMemoryAllocation.doc: The API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory or other resources to perform the requested operation.

cudaErrorInitializationError.doc: The API call failed because the CUDA driver and runtime could not be initialized.

cudaErrorCudartUnloading.doc:
This indicates that a CUDA Runtime API call cannot be executed because it is being called during process shut down, at a point
in time after CUDA driver has been unloaded.

cudaErrorProfilerDisabled.doc:
This indicates profiler is not initialized for this run. This can happen when the application is running with external profiling
tools like visual profiler.

cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration.doc:
This indicates that a kernel launch is requesting resources that can never be satisfied by the current device. Requesting
more shared memory per block than the device supports will trigger this error, as will requesting too many threads or blocks.
See `cudaDeviceProp` for more device limitations.

cudaErrorVersionTranslation.doc:
This indicates that the driver is newer than the runtime version and returned graph node parameter information that the runtime
does not understand and is unable to translate.

cudaErrorInvalidPitchValue.doc:
This indicates that one or more of the pitch-related parameters passed to the API call is not within the acceptable range
for pitch.

cudaErrorInvalidSymbol.doc: This indicates that the symbol name/identifier passed to the API call is not a valid name or identifier.

cudaErrorInvalidHostPointer.doc: This indicates that at least one host pointer passed to the API call is not a valid host pointer.

cudaErrorInvalidDevicePointer.doc: This indicates that at least one device pointer passed to the API call is not a valid device pointer.

cudaErrorInvalidTexture.doc: This indicates that the texture passed to the API call is not a valid texture.

cudaErrorInvalidTextureBinding.doc:
This indicates that the texture binding is not valid. This occurs if you call cudaGetTextureAlignmentOffset() with an unbound
```text
texture.
```

cudaErrorInvalidChannelDescriptor.doc:
This indicates that the channel descriptor passed to the API call is not valid. This occurs if the format is not one of the
formats specified by `cudaChannelFormatKind`, or if one of the dimensions is invalid.

cudaErrorInvalidMemcpyDirection.doc: This indicates that the direction of the memcpy passed to the API call is not one of the types specified by `cudaMemcpyKind`.

cudaErrorAddressOfConstant.doc:
via [cudaGetSymbolAddress()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/memory-management.html#group__CUDART__MEMORY_1g4f513be54d3794667c2017146b3d6a2b "Finds the address associated with a CUDA symbol.").

This indicated that the user has taken the address of a constant variable, which was forbidden up until the CUDA 3.1 release.

cudaErrorTextureFetchFailed.doc:
This indicated that a texture fetch was not able to be performed. This was previously used for device emulation of texture
```text
operations.
```

cudaErrorTextureNotBound.doc: This indicated that a texture was not bound for access. This was previously used for device emulation of texture operations.

cudaErrorSynchronizationError.doc: This indicated that a synchronization operation had failed. This was previously used for some device emulation functions.

cudaErrorInvalidFilterSetting.doc: This indicates that a non-float texture was being accessed with linear filtering. This is not supported by CUDA.

cudaErrorInvalidNormSetting.doc: This indicates that an attempt was made to read an unsupported data type as a normalized float. This is not supported by CUDA.

cudaErrorMixedDeviceExecution.doc: Mixing of device and device emulation code was not allowed.

cudaErrorNotYetImplemented.doc: This indicates that the API call is not yet implemented. Production releases of CUDA will never return this error.

cudaErrorMemoryValueTooLarge.doc: This indicated that an emulated device pointer exceeded the 32-bit address range.

cudaErrorStubLibrary.doc:
This indicates that the CUDA driver that the application has loaded is a stub library. Applications that run with the stub
rather than a real driver loaded will result in CUDA API returning this error.

cudaErrorInsufficientDriver.doc:
This indicates that the installed NVIDIA CUDA driver is older than the CUDA runtime library. This is not a supported configuration.
Users should install an updated NVIDIA display driver to allow the application to run.

cudaErrorCallRequiresNewerDriver.doc:
This indicates that the API call requires a newer CUDA driver than the one currently installed. Users should install an updated
NVIDIA CUDA driver to allow the API call to succeed.

cudaErrorInvalidSurface.doc: This indicates that the surface passed to the API call is not a valid surface.

cudaErrorDuplicateVariableName.doc:
This indicates that multiple global or constant variables (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the
same string name.

cudaErrorDuplicateTextureName.doc: This indicates that multiple textures (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

cudaErrorDuplicateSurfaceName.doc: This indicates that multiple surfaces (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

cudaErrorDevicesUnavailable.doc:
This indicates that all CUDA devices are busy or unavailable at the current time. Devices are often busy/unavailable due to
use of cudaComputeModeProhibited, cudaComputeModeExclusiveProcess, or when long running CUDA kernels have filled up the GPU and are blocking new work from starting. They can also be unavailable
due to memory constraints on a device that already has active CUDA work being performed.

cudaErrorIncompatibleDriverContext.doc:
This indicates that the current context is not compatible with this the CUDA Runtime. This can only occur if you are using
CUDA Runtime/Driver interoperability and have created an existing Driver context using the driver API. The Driver context
may be incompatible either because the Driver context was created using an older version of the API, because the Runtime API
call expects a primary driver context and the Driver context is not primary, or because the Driver context has been destroyed.
Please see [Interactions](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/driver-interactions.html#group__CUDART__DRIVER) with the CUDA Driver API" for more information.

cudaErrorMissingConfiguration.doc: The device function being invoked (usually via [cudaLaunchKernel()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/execution-control.html#group__CUDART__EXECUTION_1g5064cdf5d8e6741ace56fd8be951783c "Launches a device function.")) was not previously configured via the cudaConfigureCall() function.

cudaErrorPriorLaunchFailure.doc: This indicated that a previous kernel launch failed. This was previously used for device emulation of kernel launches.

cudaErrorLaunchMaxDepthExceeded.doc:
This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch did not occur because the depth of the child grid would exceed the
maximum supported number of nested grid launches.

cudaErrorLaunchFileScopedTex.doc:
This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped textures which are unsupported by
the device runtime. Kernels launched via the device runtime only support textures created with the Texture Object API's.

cudaErrorLaunchFileScopedSurf.doc:
This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped surfaces which are unsupported by
the device runtime. Kernels launched via the device runtime only support surfaces created with the Surface Object API's.

cudaErrorSyncDepthExceeded.doc:
This error indicates that a call to `cudaDeviceSynchronize` made from the device runtime failed because the call was made at grid depth greater than than either the default (2 levels
of grids) or user specified device limit cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth. To be able to synchronize on launched grids at a greater depth successfully, the maximum nested depth at which `cudaDeviceSynchronize` will be called must be specified with the cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth limit to the `cudaDeviceSetLimit` api before the host-side launch of a kernel using the device runtime. Keep in mind that additional levels of sync depth require
the runtime to reserve large amounts of device memory that cannot be used for user allocations. Note that `cudaDeviceSynchronize` made from device runtime is only supported on devices of compute capability < 9.0.

cudaErrorLaunchPendingCountExceeded.doc:
This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch failed because the launch would exceed the limit cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount. For this launch to proceed successfully, `cudaDeviceSetLimit` must be called to set the cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount to be higher than the upper bound of outstanding launches that can be issued to the device runtime. Keep in mind that raising
```text
the limit of pending device runtime launches will require the runtime to reserve device memory that cannot be used for user
allocations.
```

cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction.doc: The requested device function does not exist or is not compiled for the proper device architecture.

cudaErrorNoDevice.doc: This indicates that no CUDA-capable devices were detected by the installed CUDA driver.

cudaErrorInvalidDevice.doc:
This indicates that the device ordinal supplied by the user does not correspond to a valid CUDA device or that the action
requested is invalid for the specified device.

cudaErrorDeviceNotLicensed.doc: This indicates that the device doesn't have a valid Grid License.

cudaErrorSoftwareValidityNotEstablished.doc:
By default, the CUDA runtime may perform a minimal set of self-tests, as well as CUDA driver tests, to establish the validity
of both. Introduced in CUDA 11.2, this error return indicates that at least one of these tests has failed and the validity
of either the runtime or the driver could not be established.

cudaErrorStartupFailure.doc: This indicates an internal startup failure in the CUDA runtime.

cudaErrorInvalidKernelImage.doc: This indicates that the device kernel image is invalid.

cudaErrorDeviceUninitialized.doc:
This most frequently indicates that there is no context bound to the current thread. This can also be returned if the context
passed to an API call is not a valid handle (such as a context that has had [cuCtxDestroy()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__CUDA__CTX_1g27a365aebb0eb548166309f58a1e8b8e) invoked on it). This can also be returned if a user mixes different API versions (i.e. 3010 context with 3020 API calls).
See [cuCtxGetApiVersion()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__CUDA__CTX_1g088a90490dafca5893ef6fbebc8de8fb) for more details.

cudaErrorMapBufferObjectFailed.doc: This indicates that the buffer object could not be mapped.

cudaErrorUnmapBufferObjectFailed.doc: This indicates that the buffer object could not be unmapped.

cudaErrorArrayIsMapped.doc: This indicates that the specified array is currently mapped and thus cannot be destroyed.

cudaErrorAlreadyMapped.doc: This indicates that the resource is already mapped.

cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice.doc:
This indicates that there is no kernel image available that is suitable for the device. This can occur when a user specifies
code generation options for a particular CUDA source file that do not include the corresponding device configuration.

cudaErrorAlreadyAcquired.doc: This indicates that a resource has already been acquired.

cudaErrorNotMapped.doc: This indicates that a resource is not mapped.

cudaErrorNotMappedAsArray.doc: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as an array.

cudaErrorNotMappedAsPointer.doc: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as a pointer.

cudaErrorECCUncorrectable.doc: This indicates that an uncorrectable ECC error was detected during execution.

cudaErrorUnsupportedLimit.doc: This indicates that the `cudaLimit` passed to the API call is not supported by the active device.

cudaErrorDeviceAlreadyInUse.doc: This indicates that a call tried to access an exclusive-thread device that is already in use by a different thread.

cudaErrorPeerAccessUnsupported.doc: This error indicates that P2P access is not supported across the given devices.

cudaErrorInvalidPtx.doc:
A PTX compilation failed. The runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary
for the current device.

cudaErrorInvalidGraphicsContext.doc: This indicates an error with the OpenGL or DirectX context.

cudaErrorNvlinkUncorrectable.doc: This indicates that an uncorrectable NVLink error was detected during the execution.

cudaErrorJitCompilerNotFound.doc:
This indicates that the PTX JIT compiler library was not found. The JIT Compiler library is used for PTX compilation. The
runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion.doc:
This indicates that the provided PTX was compiled with an unsupported toolchain. The most common reason for this, is the PTX
was generated by a compiler newer than what is supported by the CUDA driver and PTX JIT compiler.

cudaErrorJitCompilationDisabled.doc:
This indicates that the JIT compilation was disabled. The JIT compilation compiles PTX. The runtime may fall back to compiling
PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

cudaErrorUnsupportedExecAffinity.doc: This indicates that the provided execution affinity is not supported by the device.

cudaErrorUnsupportedDevSideSync.doc: This indicates that the code to be compiled by the PTX JIT contains unsupported call to cudaDeviceSynchronize.

cudaErrorContained.doc:
This indicates that an exception occurred on the device that is now contained by the GPU's error containment capability. Common
causes are - a. Certain types of invalid accesses of peer GPU memory over nvlink b. Certain classes of hardware errors This
leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA,
the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorInvalidSource.doc: This indicates that the device kernel source is invalid.

cudaErrorFileNotFound.doc: This indicates that the file specified was not found.

cudaErrorSharedObjectSymbolNotFound.doc: This indicates that a link to a shared object failed to resolve.

cudaErrorSharedObjectInitFailed.doc: This indicates that initialization of a shared object failed.

cudaErrorOperatingSystem.doc: This error indicates that an OS call failed.

cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle.doc: This indicates that a resource handle passed to the API call was not valid. Resource handles are opaque types like `cudaStream_t` and `cudaEvent_t`.

cudaErrorIllegalState.doc: This indicates that a resource required by the API call is not in a valid state to perform the requested operation.

cudaErrorLossyQuery.doc:
This indicates an attempt was made to introspect an object in a way that would discard semantically important information.
This is either due to the object using funtionality newer than the API version used to introspect it or omission of optional
return arguments.

cudaErrorSymbolNotFound.doc:
This indicates that a named symbol was not found. Examples of symbols are global/constant variable names, driver function
names, texture names, and surface names.

cudaErrorNotReady.doc:
This indicates that asynchronous operations issued previously have not completed yet. This result is not actually an error,
but must be indicated differently than cudaSuccess (which indicates completion). Calls that may return this value include `cudaEventQuery` and `cudaStreamQuery`.

cudaErrorIllegalAddress.doc:
The device encountered a load or store instruction on an invalid memory address. This leaves the process in an inconsistent
state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources.doc:
This indicates that a launch did not occur because it did not have appropriate resources. Although this error is similar to
cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration, this error usually indicates that the user has attempted to pass too many arguments to the device kernel, or the kernel
launch specifies too many threads for the kernel's register count.

cudaErrorLaunchTimeout.doc:
This indicates that the device kernel took too long to execute. This can only occur if timeouts are enabled - see the device
attribute cudaDevAttrKernelExecTimeout for more information. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error.
To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorLaunchIncompatibleTexturing.doc: This error indicates a kernel launch that uses an incompatible texturing mode.

cudaErrorPeerAccessAlreadyEnabled.doc: This error indicates that a call to `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess` is trying to re-enable peer addressing on from a context which has already had peer addressing enabled.

cudaErrorPeerAccessNotEnabled.doc: This error indicates that `cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess` is trying to disable peer addressing which has not been enabled yet via `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess`.

cudaErrorSetOnActiveProcess.doc:
This indicates that the user has called `cudaSetValidDevices`, `cudaSetDeviceFlags`, `cudaD3D9SetDirect3DDevice`, `cudaD3D10SetDirect3DDevice`, `cudaD3D11SetDirect3DDevice`, or `cudaVDPAUSetVDPAUDevice` after initializing the CUDA runtime by calling non-device management operations (allocating memory and launching kernels
are examples of non-device management operations). This error can also be returned if using runtime/driver interoperability
and there is an existing [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) active on the host thread.

cudaErrorContextIsDestroyed.doc: This error indicates that the context current to the calling thread has been destroyed using [cuCtxDestroy](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__CUDA__CTX_1g27a365aebb0eb548166309f58a1e8b8e), or is a primary context which has not yet been initialized.

cudaErrorAssert.doc:
An assert triggered in device code during kernel execution. The device cannot be used again. All existing allocations are
invalid. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorTooManyPeers.doc:
This error indicates that the hardware resources required to enable peer access have been exhausted for one or more of the
devices passed to cudaEnablePeerAccess().

cudaErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered.doc: This error indicates that the memory range passed to `cudaHostRegister` has already been registered.

cudaErrorHostMemoryNotRegistered.doc: This error indicates that the pointer passed to `cudaHostUnregister` does not correspond to any currently registered memory region.

cudaErrorHardwareStackError.doc:
Device encountered an error in the call stack during kernel execution, possibly due to stack corruption or exceeding the stack
size limit. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue
using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorIllegalInstruction.doc:
The device encountered an illegal instruction during kernel execution This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and
any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorMisalignedAddress.doc:
The device encountered a load or store instruction on a memory address which is not aligned. This leaves the process in an
inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated
and relaunched.

cudaErrorInvalidAddressSpace.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered an instruction which can only operate on memory locations in certain address
spaces (global, shared, or local), but was supplied a memory address not belonging to an allowed address space. This leaves
the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process
must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorInvalidPc.doc:
The device encountered an invalid program counter. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work
will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorLaunchFailure.doc:
An exception occurred on the device while executing a kernel. Common causes include dereferencing an invalid device pointer
and accessing out of bounds shared memory. Less common cases can be system specific - more information about these cases can
be found in the system specific user guide. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will
return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorCooperativeLaunchTooLarge.doc: This error indicates that the number of blocks launched per grid for a kernel that was launched via either [cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/high-level-api.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g7c4cb6c44a6c4608da36c44374499b31 "Launches a device function.") exceeds the maximum number of blocks as allowed by [cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/high-level-api.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g5a5d67a3c907371559ba692195e8a38c "Returns occupancy for a device function.") or [cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessorWithFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/high-level-api.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g603b86b20b37823253ff89fe8688ba83 "Returns occupancy for a device function with the specified flags.") times the number of multiprocessors as specified by the device attribute cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount.

cudaErrorTensorMemoryLeak.doc:
An exception occurred on the device while exiting a kernel using tensor memory: the tensor memory was not completely deallocated.
This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA,
the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorNotPermitted.doc: This error indicates the attempted operation is not permitted.

cudaErrorNotSupported.doc: This error indicates the attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

cudaErrorSystemNotReady.doc:
This error indicates that the system is not yet ready to start any CUDA work. To continue using CUDA, verify the system configuration
is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are actively running. More information about this error can be found in
the system specific user guide.

cudaErrorSystemDriverMismatch.doc:
This error indicates that there is a mismatch between the versions of the display driver and the CUDA driver. Refer to the
compatibility documentation for supported versions.

cudaErrorCompatNotSupportedOnDevice.doc:
This error indicates that the system was upgraded to run with forward compatibility but the visible hardware detected by CUDA
does not support this configuration. Refer to the compatibility documentation for the supported hardware matrix or ensure
that only supported hardware is visible during initialization via the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable.

cudaErrorMpsConnectionFailed.doc: This error indicates that the MPS client failed to connect to the MPS control daemon or the MPS server.

cudaErrorMpsRpcFailure.doc: This error indicates that the remote procedural call between the MPS server and the MPS client failed.

cudaErrorMpsServerNotReady.doc:
This error indicates that the MPS server is not ready to accept new MPS client requests. This error can be returned when the
MPS server is in the process of recovering from a fatal failure.

cudaErrorMpsMaxClientsReached.doc: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to create MPS client have been exhausted.

cudaErrorMpsMaxConnectionsReached.doc: This error indicates the hardware resources required to device connections have been exhausted.

cudaErrorMpsClientTerminated.doc:
This error indicates that the MPS client has been terminated by the server. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated
and relaunched.

cudaErrorCdpNotSupported.doc:
This error indicates, that the program is using CUDA Dynamic Parallelism, but the current configuration, like MPS, does not
support it.

cudaErrorCdpVersionMismatch.doc: This error indicates, that the program contains an unsupported interaction between different versions of CUDA Dynamic Parallelism.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported.doc: The operation is not permitted when the stream is capturing.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated.doc: The current capture sequence on the stream has been invalidated due to a previous error.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureMerge.doc: The operation would have resulted in a merge of two independent capture sequences.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnmatched.doc: The capture was not initiated in this stream.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnjoined.doc: The capture sequence contains a fork that was not joined to the primary stream.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureIsolation.doc:
A dependency would have been created which crosses the capture sequence boundary. Only implicit in-stream ordering dependencies
are allowed to cross the boundary.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureImplicit.doc: The operation would have resulted in a disallowed implicit dependency on a current capture sequence from cudaStreamLegacy.

cudaErrorCapturedEvent.doc: The operation is not permitted on an event which was last recorded in a capturing stream.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureWrongThread.doc: A stream capture sequence not initiated with the cudaStreamCaptureModeRelaxed argument to `cudaStreamBeginCapture` was passed to `cudaStreamEndCapture` in a different thread.

cudaErrorTimeout.doc: This indicates that the wait operation has timed out.

cudaErrorGraphExecUpdateFailure.doc:
This error indicates that the graph update was not performed because it included changes which violated constraints specific
to instantiated graph update.

cudaErrorExternalDevice.doc:
This indicates that an error has occurred in a device outside of GPU. It can be a synchronous error with respect to CUDA API or an
asynchronous error from the external device. In case of asynchronous error, it means that if CUDA was waiting for an external
device's signal before consuming shared data, the external device signaled an error indicating that the data is not valid
for consumption. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To
continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched. In case of synchronous error, it means that one or more
external devices have encountered an error and cannot complete the operation.

cudaErrorInvalidClusterSize.doc: This indicates that a kernel launch error has occurred due to cluster misconfiguration.

cudaErrorFunctionNotLoaded.doc: Indiciates a function handle is not loaded when calling an API that requires a loaded function.

cudaErrorInvalidResourceType.doc: This error indicates one or more resources passed in are not valid resource types for the operation.

cudaErrorInvalidResourceConfiguration.doc: This error indicates one or more resources are insufficient or non-applicable for the operation.

cudaErrorStreamDetached.doc:
This error indicates that the requested operation is not permitted because the stream is in a detached state. This can occur
if the green context associated with the stream has been destroyed, limiting the stream's operational capabilities.

cudaErrorGraphRecaptureFailure.doc: This error indicates that a graph recapture failed and had to be terminated.

cudaErrorUnknown.doc: This indicates that an unknown internal error has occurred.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueFd.doc: Handle is an opaque file descriptor.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueWin32.doc: Handle is an opaque shared NT handle.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueWin32K.doc: Handle is an opaque, globally shared handle.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeD3D12Heap.doc: Handle is a D3D12 heap object.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeD3D12Resourc.doc: Handle is a D3D12 committed resource.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeD3D11Resourc.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle to a D3D11 resource.
Handle is a globally shared handle to a D3D11 resource.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeOpaqueFd.doc: Handle is an opaque file descriptor.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeOpaqueWin.doc: Handle is an opaque shared NT handle.
Handle is an opaque, globally shared handle.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeD3D12Fenc.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle referencing a D3D12 fence object.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeD3D11Fenc.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle referencing a D3D11 fence object.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeKeyedMute.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle referencing a D3D11 keyed mutex object.
Handle is a shared KMT handle referencing a D3D11 keyed mutex object.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeTimelineS.doc: Handle is an opaque handle file descriptor referencing a timeline semaphore.
Handle is an opaque handle file descriptor referencing a timeline semaphore.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesOptions.doc: CUDA GPUDirect RDMA flush writes APIs supported on the device.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesOptionHost.doc: `cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites` and its CUDA Driver API counterpart are supported on the device.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesOptionMemOps.doc: The [CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_FLUSH](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1ggf16864e8693d888f8178067470001b215dd93e7173619c943fae495568f4d771) flag and the [CU_STREAM_MEM_OP_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1ggb257b534afdb704b6ebdb99c16a5b292d4e126a89b57ebf4a213ee1774ed103f) MemOp are supported on the CUDA device.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesScope.doc: CUDA GPUDirect RDMA flush writes scopes.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesToOwner.doc: Blocks until remote writes are visible to the CUDA device context owning the data.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesToAllDevices.doc: Blocks until remote writes are visible to all CUDA device contexts.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesTarget.doc: CUDA GPUDirect RDMA flush writes targets.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesTargetCurren.doc: Sets the target for `cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites` to the currently active CUDA device context.

cudaFuncAttribute.doc: CUDA function attributes that can be set using [cudaFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/high-level-api.html#group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL_1g61085e9f04656b92573af16072bbc78d "[C++ API] Set attributes for a given function").

cudaFuncAttributeClusterDimMustBeSet.doc: Indicator to enforce valid cluster dimension specification on kernel launch.

cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeA.doc: Whether non-portable cluster scheduling policy is supported.

cudaFuncCachePreferNone.doc: Default function cache configuration, no preference.

cudaFuncCachePreferShared.doc: Prefer larger shared memory and smaller L1 cache.

cudaFuncCachePreferL1.doc: Prefer larger L1 cache and smaller shared memory.

cudaFuncCachePreferEqual.doc: Prefer equal size L1 cache and shared memory.

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrdering.doc: CUDA GPUDirect RDMA flush writes ordering features of the device.

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrderingNone.doc:
The device does not natively support ordering of GPUDirect RDMA writes. cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites() can be leveraged if
```text
supported.
```

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrderingOwner.doc: Natively, the device can consistently consume GPUDirect RDMA writes, although other CUDA devices may not.

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrderingAllDevice.doc: Any CUDA device in the system can consistently consume GPUDirect RDMA writes to this device.

cudaGetDriverEntryPointFlags.doc: Flags to specify search options to be used with `cudaGetDriverEntryPoint` For more details see [cuGetProcAddress](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__DRIVER__ENTRY__POINT.html#group__CUDA__DRIVER__ENTRY__POINT_1gcae5adad00590572ab35b2508c2d6e0d).

cudaEnableDefault.doc: Default search mode for driver symbols.

cudaEnableLegacyStream.doc: Search for legacy versions of driver symbols.

cudaEnablePerThreadDefaultStream.doc: Search for per-thread versions of driver symbols.

cudaGraphChildGraphOwnershipClone.doc:
Default behavior for a child graph node. Child graph is cloned into the parent and memory allocation/free nodes can't be present
in the child graph.

cudaGraphChildGraphOwnershipMove.doc:
The child graph is moved to the parent. The handle to the child graph is owned by the parent and will be destroyed when the
```text
parent is destroyed.The following restrictions apply to child graphs after they have been moved: Cannot be independently instantiated
or destroyed; Cannot be added as a child graph of a separate parent graph; Cannot be used as an argument to cudaGraphExecUpdate;
Cannot have additional memory allocation or free nodes added.
```

cudaGraphChildGraphOwnershipInvalid.doc: Invalid ownership flag. Set when params are queried to prevent accidentally reusing the driver-owned graph object.

cudaGraphCondTypeIf.doc: Conditional 'if/else' Node. Body[0] executed if condition is non-zero. If size == 2, an optional ELSE graph is created and this is executed if the condition is zero.

cudaGraphCondTypeWhile.doc: Conditional 'while' Node. Body executed repeatedly while condition value is non-zero.

cudaGraphCondTypeSwitch.doc:
Conditional 'switch' Node. Body[n] is executed once, where 'n' is the value of the condition. If the condition does not match
a body index, no body is launched.

Max number of registers that a thread may use.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitThreadsPerBlock.doc:
IN: Specifies minimum number of threads per block to target compilation for
OUT: Returns the number of threads the compiler actually targeted. This restricts the resource utilization of the compiler
(e.g. max registers) such that a block with the given number of threads should be able to launch based on register limitations.
Note, this option does not currently take into account any other resource limitations, such as shared memory utilization.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitWallTime.doc:

cudaJitOptimizationLevel.doc:
Level of optimizations to apply to generated code (0 - 4), with 4 being the default and highest level of optimizations.

cudaJitFallbackStrategy.doc:
Specifies choice of fallback strategy if matching cubin is not found. Choice is based on supplied `cudaJit_Fallback`. Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type `cudaJit_Fallback`
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitGenerateDebugInfo.doc:

cudaJitLogVerbose.doc:

cudaJitCacheMode.doc:
Specifies whether to enable caching explicitly (-dlcm)
Choice is based on supplied `cudaJit_CacheMode`.

cudaJitPositionIndependentCode.doc:

cudaJitMinCtaPerSm.doc:
This option hints to the JIT compiler the minimum number of CTAs from the kernel’s grid to be mapped to a SM. This option
is ignored when used together with cudaJitMaxRegisters or cudaJitThreadsPerBlock. Optimizations based on this option need cudaJitMaxThreadsPerBlock to be specified as well. For kernels already using PTX directive .minnctapersm, this option will be ignored by default. Use
cudaJitOverrideDirectiveValues to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitMaxThreadsPerBlock.doc:
Maximum number threads in a thread block, computed as the product of the maximum extent specifed for each dimension of the
block. This limit is guaranteed not to be exeeded in any invocation of the kernel. Exceeding the maximum number of threads
results in runtime error or kernel launch failure. For kernels already using PTX directive .maxntid, this option will be ignored
by default. Use cudaJitOverrideDirectiveValues to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: int
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitOverrideDirectiveValues.doc:
This option lets the values specified using cudaJitMaxRegisters, cudaJitThreadsPerBlock, cudaJitMaxThreadsPerBlock and cudaJitMinCtaPerSm take precedence over any PTX directives. (0: Disable, default; 1: Enable) Option type: int
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaPreferPtx.doc: Prefer to compile ptx if exact binary match not found.

cudaPreferBinary.doc: Prefer to fall back to compatible binary code if exact match not found.
